contexts: The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends a country-level target to reduce NCDs by 25% by 2025 and premature deaths by 33% by 2030.

A total of 150,000 Health and Wellness Centers are proposed to be established across India to give complete primary health-care services that are equivalent to the preeminent causes of huge burden of disease, including CVDs and other NCDs (AYUSHMAN BHARAT Comprehensive Primary Health Care through Health andWellness Centers Operational Guidelines).
GOI is primarily focusing on addressing the increasing damage because of NCDs (Bhargava and Paul, 2020).

WHO's action plan aspires to counter the CVD epidemic by encouraging research work, reducing, monitoring and modifying determinants and risk factors and integrating disease prevention programs and controlling local policies under global strategy for the prevention and control of NCDs (2008-2013Action Plan for the Global Strategy for the Prevention and Control of Noncommunicable Diseases, WHO).
